subject: Mutual action plan: performance validation & streaming TTFT (initial plan)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@asterlabs.io>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@asterlabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan: performance validation & streaming TTFT (initial plan)

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — excited to move towards a performance gate as part of the MAP so your team can feel confident running live chat at scale. Attached is a concise plan (map-performance-plan.xlsx) that outlines the test phases, acceptance criteria, and proposed close timeline. High level: 

- Kickoff: 09/16 — align infra, signal test windows
- Eval sprint: 09/17-09/18 — run streaming TTFT and concurrency sweeps (warm + cold cache)
- Canary & rollout: 09/20-09/24 — 10% canary, monitor regressions, then ramp
- Target close: 10/05 (final sign-off + SOW)

Acceptance asks (proposed):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) streaming p95 <= 500ms, p99 <= 900ms under expected concurrency profile
- Sustained throughput: 4–6k tokens/sec aggregate for your expected peak concurrency pattern
- No functional regressions on the sample prompt set (we'll run your 120 prompt eval set)

We'll run tests from a Redwood dedicated cluster (us-west-2, A100-40GB). Test harness will be the same harness we used in the demo, with both cold-start and warm-KV cache passes — we'll provide raw traces and packet-level timings. Please confirm the acceptance targets above or flag any changes before EOD 09/15 so we can lock the MAP and schedule runs.

Attachments: map-performance-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), test-harness-spec.md (link in map)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(jordan_blake@redwood.com)

From: Elena Martin <elena@asterlabs.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@asterlabs.io>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance validation & streaming TTFT (initial plan)

Jordan — thanks for the clear plan and timeline. A couple clarifications from our side before you run the eval: 

1) Our primary concern is tail TTFT for newly opened chats under load. We are hoping p99 stays under ~1s for 30 concurrent agents (each agent ~1 chat stream). If you can show both p95 and p99 with cold-start and warm cache, that'll be ideal.
2) For throughput, our peak expected burst is roughly 3k tokens/sec sustained for ~5 minutes and 6k tokens/sec as a short burst. Can you confirm your throughput measurement methodology (tokens/sec aggregated vs per-worker)?
3) Do you require any firewall or IP allowlist changes for you to run tests against our staging environment?

Also, can you confirm when we'll get the raw trace files? We want to run a quick internal comparison to our telemetry.

Elena Martin
Head of Product — Aster Labs
elena@asterlabs.io

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@asterlabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance validation & streaming TTFT (initial plan)

Elena — great questions, quick answers: 

- Tail focus: we'll report TTFT p50/p95/p99 for both cold and warm runs. Cold run is no KV cache and cold backend process; warm run will be after a 5-minute priming period.
- Throughput: our CSVs report both per-worker tokens/sec and an aggregated tokens/sec across the serving pool; we'll highlight the aggregate in the summary and include per-worker breakdown for reproducibility.
- Network: no inbound to your staging required — we can run from Redwood's test harness pointing at a staging endpoint if you provide an allowlist IP range; alternatively we can run from our cluster and replay recorded client patterns if allowlist isn't possible.
- Traces: raw trace bundles (latency CSV + per-request trace.jsonl) will be uploaded within 24 hours after the sprint completes.

We're holding a short sync tomorrow (09/16) at 10:00 PT to finalize test windows — joining this call will help us lock the MAP. Invite sent separately.

Cheers,
Jordan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martin <elena@asterlabs.io>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@asterlabs.io>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mutual action plan: performance validation & streaming TTFT (initial plan) — eval results

Elena / team — we completed the eval sprint on 09/17. Summary below; raw CSV attached (latency-results-09-17.csv) and trace bundles uploaded to the Drive link in the MAP. Tests run from Redwood dedicated cluster (us-west-2, 4 x A100-40GB), model variant: redwood-stream-13b-q4-optim, sequence: 512 tokens typical. We ran three passes: cold-start, warm-start, and concurrency sweep.

Quick summary (aggregated across the serving pool):
- Cold-start TTFT (first request after cold boot): p50 420ms, p95 1,180ms, p99 2,040ms
- Warm-start TTFT (after 5-minute priming): p50 150ms, p95 430ms, p99 780ms
- Subsequent-token streaming latency (warm): p50 28ms, p95 75ms, p99 160ms
- Concurrency sweep (ramp to 50 concurrent streaming clients): sustained aggregate tokens/sec: 5,100 tps for a 5-minute steady window; peak short-burst 6,300 tps observed for 90s

Mapping to acceptance:
- Your requested p99 under ~1s at 30 concurrent agents (estimated ~2.4k aggregate tps) — warm-start p99 measured at 780ms (PASS).
- Throughput: we observed sustained aggregate >3k tps in the 30-concurrency slice; we comfortably hit your burst expectations in the cluster used for the test.

Notes & caveats:
- Cold-start p99 exceeds 1s (2s+) — this is expected for cold infra. Production mitigations: keep worker pool warm, use steady keepalive priming, and client-side retry/backoff.
- Numbers will vary slightly by model variant and sequence length; we'll include guidance in the MAP spreadsheet for recommended capacity to meet SLOs with 20% headroom.

Attachments: latency-results-09-17.csv (raw), summary-traces.tar.gz (uploaded)

Next steps: if these numbers match your expectations, we propose to move to the canary window starting 09/20. Sergio will propose a canary playbook.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@asterlabs.io>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@asterlabs.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mutual action plan: performance validation & streaming TTFT (initial plan) — canary proposal

Elena — following Neha's results, here is a short canary proposal we want to include in the MAP (attached: canary-playbook.md):

- Canary window: 09/20 00:00 PT -> 09/23 23:59 PT (72 hours)
- Traffic split: 10% of production chat traffic directed to Redwood serving pool; monitor costs and p95/p99 every 10 minutes
- SLOs during canary: warm-start p95 <= 500ms, warm p99 <= 900ms; if either metric exceeds thresholds for >3 consecutive 10m windows, automatic rollback to previous model routing
- Rollback plan: immediate 100% failover to fallback model (redwood-stream-13b-safe) + incident playbook; CS and SRE on call for first 24 hours
- Acceptance gating for full ramp: 72h canary with no SLA breaches and no more than 2 regressions requiring operator intervention

Please confirm you can accept the canary window above. If so, Jordan & I will update the MAP and circulate a DocuSign-ready MAP for signatures.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Martin <elena@asterlabs.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance validation & streaming TTFT (initial plan) — canary proposal

Sergio / Jordan / Neha — this looks good to us. We reviewed Neha's CSV and the warm-start numbers map to our telemetry — appreciate the raw traces. We accept the canary window and rollback thresholds as proposed.

We'll expect the DocuSign MAP and the final SOW; if we can sign by 10/05 we will proceed with the 10/20 production ramp date in the MAP. Attached: a signed MAP (aster-signed-map-docusign.pdf) and the HubSpot deal updated with the close target.

Thanks all — excited to get this across the finish line.

Elena Martin
Head of Product — Aster Labs
